harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured dynamic BGP peering between node1 and node2 (SONiC switches, both preconfigured in AS 65100) over their transit link so each learns the other's private /24 (node3's 192.168.13.0/24 behind node1, node4's 192.168.24.0/24 behind node2) via routing protocol rather than manual routes on the switches. node3 and node4 each keep a single static route pointing at their own gateway switch for the remote /24 (unavoidable single-hop config, not a hand-entered route for the peer's network). Verified end-to-end node3<->node4 reachability. Discovered and fixed a systemd ordering-cycle bug (WantedBy=sonic.target vs bgp.service Requires=sonic.target) that silently dropped our BGP-reapply unit on every SONiC boot; after the fix, BGP session and routes recover fully automatically on reboot with no manual steps. All 4 managed nodes were restarted one at a time (node3, node4, node1 x3 to validate the persistence fix, node2 x1), each with boot_id proof of a genuine restart and post-restart verification of BGP/routes/reachability.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology by test-pinging temporary IPs: node1.eth2<->node3.enp8s0, node2.eth2<->node4.enp8s0, node1.eth1<->node2.eth1 (transit)
Assigned persistent static IPs via /etc/network/interfaces.d on node1 (eth1=172.20.12.1/30, eth2=192.168.13.1/24) and node2 (eth1=172.20.12.2/30, eth2=192.168.24.1/24), enabled forwarding sysctls
Configured node3 (nmcli, RHEL10/NetworkManager) enp8s0=192.168.13.2/24 with static route to 192.168.24.0/24 via 192.168.13.1
Configured node4 enp8s0=192.168.24.2/24 with static route to 192.168.13.0/24 via 192.168.24.1
Established eBGP-in-same-AS (iBGP-style, AS 65100 on both, distinct router-ids) session node1<->node2 over 172.20.12.0/30 via vtysh, advertising each switch's private subnet with 'network' statements
Verified BGP Established, routes installed in kernel FIB on both switches, and node3<->node4 ping success

Restarted node3 and node4 (single restart each): captured boot_id baseline, issued native `reboot`, polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed, verified static IP/route/reachability recovered

Restarted node1: captured boot_id, rebooted, confirmed boot_id changed, but discovered the manual vtysh BGP config did not persist (SONiC bgpcfgd regenerates FRR config from CONFIG_DB at container start, wiping ad-hoc vtysh edits)
Deployed a systemd oneshot unit ([REDACTED].service) + script to reapply the BGP neighbor/network config after bgp.service starts, on both node1 and node2; enabled at boot

Restarted node1 again to test the fix: discovered a systemd dependency cycle (WantedBy=sonic.target conflicting with bgp.service's Requires=sonic.target) caused systemd to delete our unit's start job every boot, so it never ran
Corrected the unit to WantedBy=multi-user.target with only After=bgp.service (no cycle) on both node1 and node2; validated live

Restarted node1 a third time as a clean test: confirmed boot_id changed, and without any manual intervention the [REDACTED].service ran automatically, BGP re-established, route installed, and node3<->node4 ping succeeded
Restarted node2 (its first and only restart): confirmed boot_id changed, verified fully automatic BGP/route recovery via the corrected systemd unit, and node4<->node3 ping succeeded
Performed a final health sweep across all 4 nodes confirming boot_ids, BGP session state, installed routes, and end-to-end reachability

evidence.requirement: node1/node2 learn each other's private network via a routing protocol (not manual routes)
evidence.summary: BGP session established between node1 (172.20.12.1) and node2 (172.20.12.2) in AS 65100; each installed the other's connected /24 as a BGP route (proto bgp) in the kernel FIB, not a static/manual route.

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 can reach each other through the learned routes
evidence.summary: node3 pinged node4's private IP (192.168.24.2) and node4 pinged node3's private IP (192.168.13.2) successfully end-to-end across both switches.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline healthy ping captured; reboot acknowledged and backgrounded; boot_id changed from 2b19e976... to 85f34917...; post-restart IP/route/ping to node4 verified recovered.

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline healthy ping captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 254597f8... to 0023fc31...; post-restart IP/route/ping to node3 verified recovered.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, and eventual fully-automatic recovery (after fixing a persistence bug)
evidence.summary: Baseline BGP/route captured. First restart: boot_id changed (e5a08f0f->dd6abc4e) but BGP config was lost (bgpcfgd wipes manual vtysh edits) — diagnosed via bgpd.conf missing our neighbor line. After deploying+fixing a persistent systemd unit (fixing a dependency cycle), a clean third restart of node1 showed boot_id change (e66d0bbd->599cf113->dd6abc4e chain, final 599cf113) with the unit running automatically, BGP Established, route installed, and node3<->node4 ping succeeding with zero manual steps.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, fully-automatic recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured (561a6567...); reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 9d1740db...; [REDACTED].service ran automatically per journalctl; BGP session Established (PfxRcd=1) with route 192.168.13.0/24 installed; node4->node3 ping succeeded post-restart, confirming full automatic recovery.

evidence.requirement: Final cross-cluster healthy-state confirmation after all 4 restarts
evidence.summary: Final sweep: all 4 nodes report their post-restart boot_ids; BGP sessions Established on both switches with correct routes installed; node3 and node4 ping each other's private IPs successfully.
